BBB Disruption in Optic Neuritis: A Novel 
Technique of Ultracytochemical H,O, and 
lmmunocytochemical Serum Albumin Co= 
Localization 
John Guy and E. Ann Ellis, Gainesville, FL 
Disruption of the blood-brain barrier (BBB) plays a major 
role in the pathogenesis of primary CNS demyelination. While 
previous ultrastructural studies showed tracer extravasation 
into the CNS, endothelial cells and tight junctions appeared 
morphologically intact, suggesting the contribution of an unseen 
factor to functional incompetence of CNS vasculature. In order 
to simultaneously probe the role of H,O, in vascular permeabili- 
ty associated with experimental allergic encephalomyelitis 
(EAE), we utilized a novel double-labeling technique for ultracy- 
tochemical localization of endogenous H,O, followed by immuno- 
cytochemical localization of serum albumin with 10 nm colloidal 
gold. Guinea pigs with EAE were evaluated by MRI, then eutha- 
nized after Gd enhancement of the optic nerves indicated BBB 
disruption. Optic nerve ultrastructure revealed gold-labeled 
albumin in the perivascular and adjacent interstitial spaces of 
capillaries and small venules where H,O,-derived cerium per- 
hydroxide reaction product was also simultaneously evident. 
Gold-labeled albumin was confined to the intravascular spaces 
of the optic nerve in the absence of adjacent H,O,. Our results 
suggest H,O, generated by activated inflammatory cells and 
endothelial cells is necessary for BBB disruption resulting in Gd 
enhancement of the optic nerve seen on MRI. 
Study supported by R01 EY07982. 
265P 
Idiopathic lntracranial Hypertension 
Associated with Tetracycline Use in 
Fraternal Twins 
Kathy Gardner, Terry A. Cox, and Kathleen 3. Digre, Salt Lake 
City, UT 
Objectiue. We report two cases of tetracycline-induced idio- 
pathic intracranial hypertension (IIH) in fraternal twin sisters. 
Background. Obesity and recent weight gain are the only sta- 
tistically proven associations with IIH. 
Designs /Methods. Our two cases are described. Fifteen famil- 
ial cases of IIH and 24 cases of IIH associated with tetracycline 
usage, including 10 infants with bulging fontanelles, are 
reviewed from the literature. 
Results. Symptoms leading to diagnosis of IIH occurred with- 
in one week of starting tetracycline in our first case. Asympto- 
matic papilledema discovered in her twin sister also taking the 
drug resolved within 2 months of stopping antibiotic. 
Compelling supportive evidence of a true association between 
tetracycline and IIH comes from pediatric reports in the 1960s of 
10 infants developing bulging fontanelles within 12 hours to 4 
days of starting tetracycline. Among the 24 combined adult and 
pediatric cases, resolution of signs and/or symptoms occurred 
within hours to days (18/24) or weeks of stopping antibiotic. 
Rapid recurrence with reinitiation of drug occurred in 3. 
Conclusions. Tetracycline produced “idiopathic” intracranial 
hypertension in fraternal twin sisters. These cases and others 
imply an underlying genetic susceptibility in at least. some of the 
patients with this condition. 
266P 
Uhthoff’s Symptom 
Frederick E. Lepore, New Brunswick, NJ 
Objectiue. To determine prevalence, etiologies, and clinical 
characteristics of Uhthoffs symptom (US) in patients with pre- 
geniculate lesions.

Background. In 1890, Uhthoff described transient exercise- 
induced blurring of vision in 4 of 100 patients with multiple scle- 
rosis (MS). 
Methods. Fifty-eight consecutive patients with pregeniculate 
visual loss (predominantly optic neuropathies) due to MS (15), 
diverse etiologies (33), and compressive lesions (10) underwent 
neuro-ophthalmologic evaluation with perimetry. 
Results. Ten patients with US (mean age, 34.7 years) were 
significantly younger (Student’s t-test, p = 0.008) than 48 
patients without US (mean age, 46.1 years). Etiologies of visual 
loss in patients with US were MS (7 patients), aneurysm (11, 
meningioma (l), and isolated optic neuritis (1). There was a sig- 
nificant association (x’, p = 0.002) of US and MS when compared 
to other causes of visual loss. There was no significant associa- 
tion (x2) of US and central/cecocentral scotoma, visual acuity 
worse than 20/50, or binocular visual loss. 
Conclusion. US not uncommonly accompanies pregeniculate 
visual loss and was reported by 17% of patients. It occurs in 
younger patients and with diverse causes of visual loss although 
it is strongly associated with MS. US is not significantly associ- 
ated with greater severity of visual loss. 
267P 
Purely Torsional Nystagmus in a Patient 
with the Stiff-Man Syndrome: A Case Report 
Michael Quentin Stearns, Bethesda, MD; Stuart E. Sinoff, 
Washington, DC; Michael L. Rosenberg, Bethesda, MD 
Objectiue. Report of a case of stiff-man syndrome with purely 
torsional nystagmus, implying involvement of GABAergic cen- 
tral vestibular pathways. 
Background. The pathophysiology of stiff-man syndrome is 
thought to be related to an abnormality of the GABAergic inhibi- 
tion of alpha spinal motor neurons. There is experimental and 
clinical evidence that GABAergic neurons are also involved in 
central vestibular function. 
Case report. A 36-year-old male with a 2-year history of typi- 
cal stiff-man syndrome developed blurred vision. General neuro- 
logic examination showed changes of stiff-man syndrome, but 
was otherwise normal. Neuro-ophthalmologic examination 
demonstrated only a prominent pure counterclockwise torsional 
nystagmus. An enhanced MRI of the posterior fossa was normal. 
Conclusions. 1. Dysfunction of central vestibular pathways 
employing GABA as an inhibitory neurotransmitter may serve 
as a model for pure torsional nystagmus. 2. Stiff-man syndrome 
may involve GABAergic control of vestibular function as well as 
spinal alpha motor neurons. 
268P 
The Clinical Spectrum of Horizontal End-On- 
End Saccades 
Michael L. Rosenberg, Bethesda, MD 
Objectiue. To better define the spectrum of intermittent ocu- 
lar movements consisting of horizontal end-on-end saccades. 
Background. Voluntary nystagmus (VN) and ocular flutter 
are clinically indistinguishable. Some normal patients with VN- 
like eye movements deny the ability to control the movements. 
Design. Thirty-one patients with intermittent oscillopsia sec- 
ondary to horizontal end-on-end saccades were reviewed retro- 
spectively in an attempt to clinically categorize the patients.
